title: Figure AI melts its retired Figure 02 humanoid robots in a furnace in a Terminator 2 style farewell
source_used: Deseret News (full text from the fulltext folder, plus its page for the embedded X post); Figure's own blog post F.02 Decommission (figure.ai, dated 30 Sep 2026, the primary source, read in full); The Times of India and KITV read in full; Gizmodo, TechEBlog, Interesting Engineering, Tom's Hardware and Inshorts read to date the story and the Schwarzenegger exchange; NDTV Profit and Root-Nation.com returned 403 and were not read
key_facts: Figure, a US humanoid-robot company, retired most of its Figure 02 (F.02) fleet by melting the robots in a 75-ton electric arc furnace at a foundry in Imatra, Finland, and filmed it; Figure's blog post F.02 Decommission and its film on X are dated 30 Sep 2026 (Figure's blog; Gizmodo embeds the X post).

Figure says it chose melting to protect its custom-built actuators and other proprietary hardware, and that taking each robot apart would have taken staff so long it would delay its F.04 robot; the F.03 fleet is growing, so keeping F.02 no longer made sense (Figure's blog; Deseret News).

The suggestion came from Arnold Schwarzenegger, who replied 'You should melt them' to Figure CEO Brett Adcock's call for ideas for a send-off on X; the reply is dated 19 Aug 2026 (TechEBlog; the Adcock post embedded in the Deseret page carries the same date; Inshorts reported the exchange on 20 Aug). Figure says it contacted him and, when he said he wanted to be involved, it put everything in motion.

No foundry Figure contacted in the US or Mexico would let a robot with lithium-ion batteries jump into its equipment; the Imatra foundry agreed, giving the team 24 hours and six melts of about 20 minutes each before the steel formed a hard crust.

Training took place at Figure's San Jose campus: robots practised jumping off a second floor onto airbags, and an AI model trained in simulation from stunt artists' movements was meant to let them jump accurately into a bucket of molten steel at a foundry they had never visited (Figure's blog; Deseret News).

Figure says the robots ran their AI policies seamlessly despite the heat and electromagnetic fields while camera equipment and other electronics failed, and stresses that the footage is real: 'we really trained robots to jump autonomously' (Figure's blog). The Times of India and TechEBlog describe the film as also showing a robot lowered on a chain.

Schwarzenegger has a cameo in the film, which echoes the end of Terminator 2 (Deseret News, Times of India, KITV); the metal bars went back to the US and are being machined into a limited series of keepsakes, and a few F.02 units remain in storage (Figure's blog); Gizmodo and TechEBlog report pre-order prices of $500 to $1,900.

Deseret News, citing Figure, says the Figure 02 units spent over 1,200 hours in a pilot at BMW's Spartanburg plant in South Carolina, helping make some 30,000 BMW X3 cars (TechEBlog says over 1,250 hours); BMW said in June it is preparing to deploy Figure 03 there.
quote_evidence: The resounding answer came from an unlikely source: Arnold Schwarzenegger, who told us to melt them.
Figure said their disposal team had just 24 hours and six melts to get it right, and each melt had only a 20-minute window before the molten steel cooled and formed a hard crust.
In an age of AI-generated footage, it’s worth being clear: we really trained robots to jump autonomously, shipped them to Finland, and had them leap into a vat of molten steel.
why_it_matters_hint: A robot maker destroyed most of a retired humanoid fleet in a film-style stunt to protect its proprietary hardware; the claims that the jumps were autonomous and the footage real come from Figure itself.
event_date: Figure posted its film and blog post on 30 Sep 2026; Schwarzenegger's reply on X is dated 19 Aug 2026; the date of the melt in Finland is not stated; Deseret News, KITV, NDTV Profit and Root-Nation covered it on 5 Oct 2026 and the Times of India on 6 Oct 2026
notes: Credit: the pool item is Deseret News, which wrote its own report (named reporter) from Figure's blog post and film, links Figure's page and embeds Adcock's X post, so it is credited 'Deseret News reports, citing Figure'. The Times of India (6 Oct) and KITV (5 Oct video page) retell the same Figure release; NDTV Profit and Root-Nation.com returned 403 and were not read. The story is older than the window: Figure posted on 30 Sep 2026 and it was covered by TechEBlog (30 Sep, US Pacific time), Interesting Engineering (1 Oct), Mezha (1 Oct), Gizmodo (1 Oct, quotes the blog) and Tom's Hardware (4 Oct) before the 5 Oct wave; nothing new happened inside the window. Small differences between outlets: hours at BMW (Deseret over 1,200, TechEBlog over 1,250); the film shows a robot lowered on a chain (Times of India, TechEBlog) while Figure's own words are that it trained robots to jump autonomously, not that every robot jumped; Schwarzenegger's closing line is quoted as 'Hasta la vista, Figure 02' (Gizmodo) and 'Hasta la vista, F.02' (TechEBlog), so it is not used. The autonomy claim and the 'footage is real' statement rest on Figure alone; no outlet reports an independent check. Figure sells the keepsakes (Gizmodo and TechEBlog give $500 to $1,900 pre-order prices), so the film is also publicity.
